intro: Chapter 9 is a short editorial note in which **Nephi explains his two sets of plates**. He keeps one record — the **larger plates** — for the secular history of his people (the reigns of the kings, the wars and contentions), and another — these **smaller plates** — chiefly for sacred and spiritual things. Both, he notes, are called the *plates of Nephi*, after his own name. Nephi stresses that he makes this second record by **commandment of the Lord for a wise purpose** which he himself does not know, and closes by testifying that the Lord knows all things from the beginning and has power to fulfill all his words.

entries.title: Grammar: The passive voice with شدن
entries.body: Persian has no inflected passive; it pairs the **past participle** of the main verb with a form of `شدن` "to become": `خوانده می شوند` "are called" (lit. "become called"). The participle is invariable and `شدن` carries the tense, person, and mood. The present passive keeps the imperfective `می-` on `شدن`.

examples.persian: ورقه های نیفای خوانده می شوند
examples.en: they are called the plates of Nephi

entries.title: Grammar: Ezafe chains
entries.body: The **ezafe** is an unstressed `-e` (or `-ye` after a vowel) that links a noun to a following possessor or modifier — `ورقه های نیفای` "the plates **of** Nephi." The Persian Book of Mormon rarely writes it, so this guide restores it as a small superscript kasra ( ِ ). It chains down a noun phrase, each link binding the next word.

examples.en: an account of the ministry to my people

entries.closing: When the head already ends in `ۀ` (`همۀ`, `درّۀ`) or in a long vowel spelled with `ی` (`چیزهای`, `روی`), the ezafe is already written and this guide leaves it unmarked.

entries.title: Grammar: The object marker را
entries.body: The particle `را` _rā_ marks a **definite direct object** and follows the *entire* object phrase — after any ezafe chain, plural, or relative clause. Because Persian puts the verb last, `را` tells the reader that everything before it is the thing being acted on.

examples.translit: hame-ye īn čīzhā rā pedar-am ... dīd
examples.en: all these things my father saw

entries.title: Grammar: Relative clauses with که
entries.body: `که` _ke_ introduces a **relative clause** modifying the noun before it — "the plates **on which** …." The head noun often carries an indefinite `-ی` (`ورقه هایی که` "plates that"), and a resumptive phrase (`بر آنها` "upon them") stands inside the clause pointing back to it.

examples.translit: varaqe-hā-yī ke man sargozašt-e kāmel-ī ... bar ānhā mī-negāram

entries.title: Grammar: Necessity with باید / می بایستی
entries.body: Obligation is expressed with the impersonal `باید` "must" (here the older, fuller `می بایستی` "it was needful that") followed by a **subjunctive** verb: `می بایستی ... درست کنم` "that I should make." `باید` itself never inflects for person; the following verb carries person and mood.

examples.persian: می بایستی این ورقه ها را درست کنم
examples.translit: mī-bāyestī īn varaqe-hā rā dorost konam
examples.en: that I should make these plates

entries.title: Grammar: The future tense (خواهد + short infinitive)
entries.body: Formal Persian marks the definite future with the auxiliary `خواستن` "to want" — conjugated for person (`خواهم`, `خواهی`, `خواهد` …) — followed by the **short infinitive** (the bare past stem: `شد`, `آورد`). The auxiliary comes **first** and takes no `می-`. Here it carries a compound verb: `کنده کاری خواهد شد` "shall be engraven."
entries.closing: Everyday speech usually lets the simple present carry future meaning; the `خواهد` future belongs to the formal, scriptural register.

etym.prose: `خرد` xerad "wisdom, reason" + `-مند` -mand "possessing" ([`-مند`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-mand)) + `-انه` -āne (adverbial) → "in a wise manner."

entries.title: Grammar: The subjunctive of purpose after تا
entries.body: `تا` "so that, in order to" opens a clause of **purpose**, whose verb stands in the **subjunctive** — the mood of intended action. A simple verb takes `بـ-` (`بسازم`); a compound verb usually drops it. The subjunctive never takes `می-`.

examples.persian: تا این ورقه ها را ... بسازم
